title: Change the slope

predict.q: The MPC rises from 0.6 to 0.8. Autonomous consumption stays at 40. What happens to the consumption function?

options.s: It shifts up, parallel to the old line.
options.fb: A parallel shift is a change in autonomous consumption; the MPC is the slope.

options.s: It pivots up from the same intercept, becoming steeper.
options.fb: The intercept stays at 40 and the slope rises from 0.6 to 0.8: the line pivots up.

options.s: It shifts down, because people save less.
options.fb: A higher MPC means more of each extra unit is spent, so C is higher at every income above zero.

options.s: It does not change, because autonomous consumption is unchanged.
options.fb: The intercept stays fixed, but the slope (MPC) changes the whole line.

task: Move the MPC slider to 0.8 and watch the slope; then move the autonomous consumption slider and watch the intercept.

target.do: Move the MPC slider to 0.8 (autonomous consumption 40), then press Check.

takeaway: The MPC sets the slope; autonomous consumption sets the intercept.
